The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['been'] and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Present Perfect tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Present Perfect.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object.

For example:

A new horse has been bought by Arya. (Passive Voice)

Arya has bought a new horse. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): The famous artist has painted a beautiful portrait of the entire family over the past few months.

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.question: A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice and mark your answer. Kartikey reported that Shivmohan was staying in Los Angeles at that time.
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice and mark your answer.

Kartikey reported that Shivmohan was staying in Los Angeles at that time.

options.text: Shivmohan reported that Kartikey was being stayed in Los Angeles at that time.
options.html: Shivmohan reported that Kartikey was being stayed in Los Angeles at that time.

options.text: Shivmohan was reported to have been stayed in Los Angeles by Kartikey at that time.
options.html: Shivmohan was reported to have been stayed in Los Angeles by Kartikey at that time.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

The options except (b) dont follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: "Shivmohan was reported to be staying in Los Angeles by Kartikey at that time."

Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

options.html: The journalist reported that the minister (1)

options.html: and refused to comment the issue to the press on (4)

questions.solution:
Part (4) contains the error.

The phrase "comment the issue to the press on" ends with an unnecessary and incorrect preposition "on."

The correct structure is:

- comment on the issue

- speak to the press

But the "on" in the end has no grammatical or logical function and creates a redundant preposition error.

Correct version:

"..and refused to comment on the issue to the press."

Hence, the error lies in part (4).

Note:

This error belongs to the category of prepositional redundancy, where a preposition appears without any syntactic role.

Common examples:

discuss about (incorrect → discuss)

mention about (incorrect → mention)

return back (incorrect → return)

Such extra prepositions distort idiomatic correctness.

questions.question: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence. You should return the report earlier if you wanted it to be useful.

questions.solution:
The grammar concept of "modal perfect forms for past obligation or reproach" applies here.

The highlighted part is wrong because "should return" expresses a present obligation, but the sentence refers to a past failure ("earlier"). Past judgments require the modal perfect form modal + have + past participle, which expresses criticism of something that did not happen.

Option (a) - incorrect

Violates modal structure: a modal cannot be followed by "had." The participle "returning" further breaks the pattern.

Option (b) - incorrect

After "have," the verb must be a past participle ("returned"), not the base form.

Option (c) - incorrect

Modals always take a bare infinitive, so "returns" is ungrammatical after "should."

Option (d) - correct

Uses the full modal perfect "should have returned," which expresses reproach for a past action that did not occur.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

Note:

Modal perfects are essential for referring to unrealised past obligations:

should have + past participle

ought to have + past participle

could have / would have (for possibility or hypothesis)

Option (b): A sympathetic and serious tone evokes compassion for the subject while treating their plight with gravity. Instead, the description of Soapy's ambitions and preparations for winter has a lighthearted and ironic edge, making this option incorrect.

Option (c): A critical and disdainful tone conveys disapproval or contempt for the subject. The author does not criticize or look down on Soapy. On the contrary, Soapy's situation is portrayed with a sense of humour and irony, making this option unsuitable.

Option (d): A reflective and melancholic tone involves thoughtful sadness or nostalgia about a subject. Although there is some subtle reflection on Soapy's condition (e.g., his rejection of charity), the tone lacks deep sadness or nostalgia. Instead, it leans more toward humour and irony.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. She questioned whether I was available the next day.

questions.solution:
In such cases where the sentence takes an Interrogative form in Direct Speech, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", and "asked", etc. in Indirect Speech are changed into "said" in Direct Speech.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

If there is a question whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No", we remove the inverted commas and add the conjunction "If" or "Whether" in the Indirect Speech and the verb/s "Is/are/am/was/were" before the subject, in Direct Speech.

For example:

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the past indefinite tense. So, the tense in the Direct Speech will be in the present indefinite.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

"I" changes to "you".

"the next day" changes to "tomorrow".

"questioned whether" changes to "said".

"was" changes to "are".

Therefore, the correct answer is: "She said, "Are you available tomorrow?""

Hence, option (d) is correct.

The Cache Hierarchy (A & B)

Caches are designed to bridge the speed gap between the CPU and the RAM.

L1 Cache: This is the "Level 1" cache. It is built into each individual CPU core and is the fastest and smallest because it is physically closest to the execution units.

L3 Cache: Unlike L1 and L2 (which are usually dedicated to a single core), the L3 cache is larger and shared by all cores in a multi-core processor. It acts as a final pool of data before the CPU has to go all the way to the much slower RAM.

Specialized Registers (C & D)

Registers are even faster than L1 cache and have very specific jobs during the Instruction Cycle.

Accumulator (AC): This is a general-purpose register used for logic and math. When the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) performs an operation (like $5 + 3$), the result ($8$) is temporarily stored here.

Program Counter (PC): This is a pointer. It keeps track of where the CPU is in a program by holding the memory address of the next instruction that needs to be fetched and executed.

The Quick Access Toolbar is a feature in Microsoft Office applications, including Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and others. It provides a convenient way to access frequently used commands and functions regardless of which tab or ribbon is currently active.

The quick access toolbar contains a set of commands that are independent of the tab on the ribbon. It usually contains buttons to save, undo, redo and print.

CPI (cycles per instruction, or clocks per instruction) is the number of computer clock speed cycles that occur while a computer instruction is being executed.

The number of cycles per instruction can be reduced by using pipelining . In some superscalar processors, more than one instruction can be performed during a single clock cycle.

In a modern computer, many programs (processes) want to use the CPU at the same time. However, a single CPU core can generally only execute one instruction at a time. The Operating System (OS) uses Process Scheduling to decide which process gets to use the CPU, for how long, and in what order.

Key Components of this Function:

The Scheduler: This is the part of the OS that selects a process from the "Ready Queue" to be executed.

The Dispatcher: This is the module that actually gives control of the CPU to the selected process.

Context Switching: When the OS stops one process and starts another, it saves the current state of the first process so it can resume exactly where it left off later.
